topic: Sharp design-based borrowing frontier for nonconcurrent platform controls under bounded calendar drift. Fix ordered enrollment blocks with bounded fixed potential outcomes, a shared control, a focal arm available only on a proper block window, and known history-predictable propensities that are positive exactly on available arms. Target the window-weighted finite-population arm-versus-control contrast under a total-variation budget Gamma on fixed control block means. Characterize up to universal constants the minimax worst-case expected length among all uniformly honest randomization intervals; construct a finite-convex-program predictable-AIPW borrowing rule and bias-aware martingale interval attaining it; prove a matching all-interval randomization lower bound; and give an optimizer-based necessary-and-sufficient condition for strict improvement over concurrent-only inference, including Gamma=0 full borrowing and the vacuous-drift concurrent-only regime. Consumer: the NCC R package and Bofill Roig et al.'s ACTT calibration. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The presolve derived the exact cumulative-sum dual for the worst-case drift bias: for normalized block weights, summation by parts reduces the total-variation support function to a finite linear program in cumulative weight discrepancies, with an explicit extremal drift witness. Combining this bias with predictable bounded-martingale variation yields a finite SOCP-type upper frontier. In the three-block symmetric witness, borrowing weight x has bias x Gamma and randomization standard deviation 2M(1-x)/sqrt(n), displaying the expected borrowing phase change. Boundary checks covered Gamma=0, vacuous drift, small concurrent samples, small propensities, deterministic external controls, and parameter-diameter saturation; no literature collision was found. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Construct fuzzy priors on fixed schedules that obey the TV constraint almost surely and control the sequential observed-data likelihood ratio, thereby matching the optimized clipped bias-martingale radius uniformly for arbitrary history-adaptive propensities. EARLY KILL TEST: For three blocks with one- or two-unit block sizes and outcomes on {-M,0,M}, enumerate every assignment path and solve the exact uniformly honest variable-length-interval LP. Stop or pivot if its minimax length is not within a uniform constant of the proposed convex frontier, or if it borrows where the claimed concurrent-only modulus equality holds.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine, up to universal constants, the minimax worst-case expected length of uniformly honest randomization intervals for a window-weighted finite-population arm-versus-control contrast when nonconcurrent control block means obey a total-variation budget and assignment uses arbitrary known history-predictable propensities.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The NCC literature handles temporal comparability through regression, smoothing, or Bayesian borrowing assumptions, while adaptive-randomization theory supplies AIPW martingales without a nonconcurrent-control drift class. Gaussian modulus arguments do not directly yield an all-interval randomization lower bound. The missing proof object is a pair of fuzzy priors on bounded fixed schedules that remains inside the TV ball almost surely and has controlled mixture likelihood ratio along every adaptive assignment path. On the upper side, realized-quadratic-variation studentization must remain valid on small-variation branches after adding the deterministic TV support-function bias, and the strict-improvement claim requires a primal-dual characterization rather than compactness alone.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A theorem giving matching universal-constant upper and lower bounds for minimax expected interval length, an attaining finite-conic-program predictable-AIPW interval with a valid small-variation branch, and an optimizer-based necessary-and-sufficient condition for strict improvement over concurrent-only inference, including Gamma=0 and vacuous-drift boundaries.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The donor construction reduces a bounded finite-population minimax problem to a finite observation kernel, clipped orbit decisions, and a primal-dual saddle system. Its first proof step does not transfer automatically: platform observations are ordered adaptive histories with availability-induced propensity zeros, and the action is a variable-length interval constrained by simultaneous coverage over every TV-admissible schedule. open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing NCC work isolates interim-analysis bias for particular regression estimators, while adaptive-AIPW confidence sequences assume a martingale centered at the target. Predictable off-window borrowing instead introduces a time-indexed worst-case drift bias. The first proof step that changes is the exponential-supermartingale construction: the sharp cumulative TV support function must be deducted pathwise before Ville-type control applies, and an online optimizer must balance this bias against randomization variation. The literature supplies neither this joint construction nor a sequential lower bound for stopping-time width.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A time-uniform coverage theorem for a predictable-AIPW borrowing confidence sequence, a finite online convex program for its weights, and matching lower bounds for worst-case width at stopping times over the TV-bounded fixed-schedule class.

method_exemplars.technique: Combine adaptive AIPW influence terms with asymptotic and nonasymptotic confidence-sequence constructions under changing policies.

method_exemplars.technique: Build mixture and stitched empirical-Bernstein boundaries from nonnegative supermartingales.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The bounded randomization increments fit its framework after sharply compensating the predictable borrowing drift.

open_problems.why_unsolved: ACTT evidence shows that the empirically relevant drift magnitude is consequential, but observed pre-window control changes do not by themselves bound the unobserved fixed-schedule contrast producing NCC bias. Estimating Gamma and then selecting borrowing weights can therefore undercover. Gaussian adaptation results do not settle the design-based problem because the ordered between-class modulus must be computed between adaptive randomization laws induced by fixed schedules in different TV balls, with zero focal-arm propensity off-window.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A theorem either constructing a single uniformly honest Gamma-indexed interval procedure whose expected length matches the known-Gamma convex frontier within a stated factor or proving a between-class-modulus lower bound that quantifies the necessary adaptation penalty.

writing_exemplar.why: Its ACTT-calibrated bias-versus-efficiency narrative naturally motivates reporting a sensitivity path rather than choosing one unverifiable drift value.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: ACTT supplies realistic nonconcurrent controls -> pooling promises precision gains -> plausible temporal heterogeneity inflates error -> determine whether honest inference can adapt across drift budgets

method_exemplars.technique: Use ordered and between-class moduli to lower-bound expected length under honesty over a union of nested classes and construct constant-factor adaptive intervals when geometry permits.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The Gamma-indexed TV balls are nested convex schedule classes, making the requested oracle-versus-honesty tradeoff an adaptive expected-length problem.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct fixed-class bias-aware intervals from a worst-case bias-standard-deviation optimizer and derive efficiency bounds against all honest intervals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the known-class oracle at each Gamma and a template for showing why data-dependent tuning cannot discard worst-case bias.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Strong-error-control platform designs generally use concurrent controls, while NCC analyses optimize or evaluate treatment-control comparisons separately. With overlapping focal windows, the same control assignments enter several contrasts, coupling covariance and drift bias. The scalar cumulative-weight-discrepancy dual becomes a vector support function, and separately optimized armwise weights need not minimize maximum expected length or preserve simultaneous coverage. Existing online-error and NCC operating-characteristic studies do not provide a finite-population conic frontier or matching simultaneous lower bound.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A multivariate finite convex program producing shared-control borrowing weights and a simultaneous randomization region with strong familywise coverage, together with a matching minimax lower bound for maximum or weighted-sum expected armwise lengths and a criterion for strict improvement over concurrent-only regions.

writing_exemplar.why: It clearly motivates adding arms while retaining strong joint error control and exposes the current concurrent-control boundary.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Platforms add arms over stages -> shared-control comparisons create multiplicity -> confirmatory use requires strong joint error control -> determine whether bounded-drift NCC borrowing can shorten all intervals honestly

method_exemplars.technique: Use vector-valued finite-population AIPW martingale arrays and design-based covariance estimators to form multivariate confidence sets.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The destination object is a vector of causal contrasts sharing assignments and controls, requiring the same joint AIPW covariance argument plus drift compensation.

method_exemplars.technique: Use vector and matrix martingale concentration with mixture-boundary constructions for simultaneous control.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Joint platform inference must control correlated contrast processes without losing all shared-control efficiency through separate scalar bounds.

method_exemplars.technique: Allocate error sequentially across entering platform hypotheses using group-sequential LOND spending.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the platform-level error-allocation structure to be coupled with valid drift-aware randomization statistics.

literature_map:
1. Lee and Wason (2020, BMC Medical Research Methodology) introduced frequentist NCC time adjustment and framed the basic power-versus-time-trend tradeoff.
2. Bofill Roig et al. (2022, BMC Medical Research Methodology; arXiv:2112.06574) found validity under equal additive trends and failures under heterogeneous or wrong-scale trends.
3. Saville et al. (2022, Clinical Trials) proposed the Bayesian Time Machine, whose gains depend on calendar-bucket and prior choices.
4. Marschner and Schou (2022, Clinical Trials) separated stagewise randomized information from cross-stage nonrandomized information.
5. Overbey, Cheung, and Bagiella (2022, Contemporary Clinical Trials) studied late-entry arms under parameter drift within model-based rather than design-based minimax inference.
6. Bofill Roig et al. (2023, Trials; arXiv:2211.09547) catalogued NCC methods and emphasized unsettled assumptions, estimands, and regulatory acceptability.
7. Krotka et al. (2023, SoftwareX; arXiv:2302.12634) implemented the NCC R package, providing a direct downstream consumer for an optimizer-derived borrowing rule.
8. Marschner (2024, Biometrical Journal) emphasized distinguishing concurrent randomized evidence from nonrandomized NCC evidence.
9. Greenstreet et al. (2024, Statistics in Medicine; arXiv:2112.06195) obtained strong FWER control for preplanned arm addition while using concurrent controls.
10. Bonnett, Potter, and Dodd (2025, Clinical Trials; DOI:10.1177/17407745251313928) calibrated NCC analyses to ACTT and documented an applied bias-efficiency tradeoff.
11. Krotka et al. (2025/2026, Statistics in Biopharmaceutical Research; arXiv:2407.13546) compared NCC treatment-control methods under time trends but did not provide a design-based minimax frontier.
12. Krotka, Posch, and Bofill Roig (2026, Statistics in Medicine; arXiv:2509.08795) showed that interim stopping can bias later-arm NCC adjustment.
13. Li and Zhao (2026; arXiv:2602.21998), Hadad et al. (2021; arXiv:1911.02768), and Cook, Mishler, and Ramdas (2024; arXiv:2311.18274) provide adaptive AIPW martingale inference without drift-aware NCC minimax theory.
14. Donoho (1994), Cai and Low (2004; arXiv:math/0503662), and Armstrong and Kolesar (2018; arXiv:1511.06028) provide modulus and bias-aware interval theory in Gaussian experiments; the unresolved bridge is an adaptive-randomization all-interval lower bound.
15. Zehetmayer, Posch, and Koenig (2022; arXiv:2112.10619) address sequential platform multiplicity, but not simultaneous design-based NCC intervals under bounded drift.
